CivicAlign · Team 9993
Imagine you live, work or travel through Parramatta CBD South. The plan proposes a new square by the station, with room for both night markets and everyday use. How should that limited space work for everyone? That is the question CivicAlign helps people explore.

CivicAlign · Team 9994
We understood Challenge 4 as a decision-support problem: build on Council's work, focus on one place, and make one growth trade-off easier to understand. On the master plan, Phase 1 sets the broad direction for Woodhouse Square, the night-time destination and more pedestrian-friendly streets. The next design conversation is about sharing the square among markets, a clear station route, shade, seating and lighting. The master plan names these uses; it does not say how much space each gets.

CivicAlign · Team 9997
SHOW: Scroll to Results, then Your say. (Backup: this slide replays both with the prototype's own values.) SAY: Every one of the nine results is a range against the plan as drawn. With markets at fifty points, event and trade capacity goes up, but shade, stormwater, clear walking space and inclusion go down; the cost falls a little. Then residents tell Council what the square should fix first: pick a role, choose up to three, and submit. In this demo nothing is sent to Council. The split also changes who delivers: more of the square becomes events and markets that Council leads with partners.

CivicAlign · Team 9999
In the backend, Council sees the decision this tool serves, its owner, when to refresh it and the follow-on actions. It also sees how many claims are checked and how many evidence gaps remain. Each resident split is checked against the plan's own principles: with markets at fifty points, P1, P3 and P4 are flagged as not met, because clear walking space and the street edge fall below the minimum. The tool flags which principle is weakened; it does not decide for Council. Resident votes are grouped by persona, and groups under ten people are hidden. The 96 votes are simulated.

CivicAlign · Team 99910
Could Council help us test CivicAlign in one facilitated design session with residents, access users, traders and staff? We'd also value an introduction to the project team, and guidance on sharing the confirmed square boundary, walking and access evidence, shade data, and any event or cost information that exists. We'll bring back a clearer storyboard and a short list of what still needs measuring. That gives Council a practical next step: a more informed conversation about the design, without pretending the prototype has already decided it. Thank you.
